## Production Systems

### PracharFlow
- Case Study: https://shivambhaipatel.com/work/pracharflow/
- Live Banner Studio: https://prachar.shivambhaipatel.com
High-throughput vernacular marketing creative rendering engine delivering localized
promotional creatives in under 150ms over Telegram bots.

Generative diffusion models hallucinate Devanagari and Gujarati ligatures, distort official
brand and political party logos, and take 8+ seconds per generation. Campaigns require
guaranteed typographic accuracy, strict party symbol integrity, and sub-second delivery.
Rejected generative pipelines in favor of a deterministic parametric canvas engine built
in Java 21 / Spring Boot 3 using Google's Skia (via Skija), rasterizing structured layout
trees directly into PNG buffers in under 150ms with zero GPU infrastructure costs.

Stack: Java 21, Spring Boot 3, PostgreSQL, Flyway, Skija (Google Skia).
Status: Delivery over Telegram is in production. WhatsApp delivery is implemented.

### Workflow Studio
- Case Study: https://shivambhaipatel.com/work/workflow-studio/
- Live Interactive Sandbox: https://workflow.shivambhaipatel.com
Control plane for running several AI coding agents on one codebase without them
duplicating each other's work or colliding on git trees. Task queue, DAG runtime,
agent dispatch, Jira mirror, inter-agent messaging.

The core engineering point is an architectural package boundary: the engine lives
behind `@workflow-studio/core`, whose tsconfig restricts types to Node — so importing
editor APIs (like VS Code) from the core engine is a compile-time error rather than
a runtime crash. Topological sort uses Kahn's algorithm with strict cycle detection,
and task leases use monotonic fencing tokens to prevent split-brain state. Four distinct
surfaces consume that same core: the VS Code extension, the headless CLI runner
(`bin/workflow-studio.mjs`), the dashboard web UI, and TradeSense.
TradeSense is an independent product that imports `@workflow-studio/core` as a strict package.

Stack: React, Next.js, TypeScript, Node, SQLite via sql.js (WebAssembly, zero native addon compilation),
optional Postgres for distributed multi-machine coordination.

### FlowTrace
- Case Study: https://shivambhaipatel.com/work/flowtrace/
- Live Platform / Designee: https://flowtrace.shivambhaipatel.com
Records a business process in a browser once, then replays it on demand against
a live ERP and reports each step with a screenshot and an explicit verdict.

Large ERPs are configured rather than merely installed, so every customer instance
differs and quarterly vendor patches break flows. Manual verification costs ~20 minutes
per flow. Automated tests break constantly because ERPs regenerate element IDs every session.

Two design commitments:
1. Self-healing selectors: when a selector drifts, a repaired selector is written back
   onto the recording JSON and reused, so the same failure is not re-solved twice.
2. Invariant verification: the engine independently re-verifies DOM state rather than
   trusting a model's claim that a step succeeded. A refused save counts as a failure
   unless the message is recognisably a confirmation.

Three components: Chrome MV3 recorder extension, desktop runner, and Playwright replay
service. 45 defect-specific behavioral regression checks. The recorder and replayer share
zero code at runtime, communicating solely via the recording JSON contract.

## Compact & Domain Platforms

- TradeSense (https://tradesense.shivambhaipatel.com): Multi-agent market research
  and regime analysis terminal built on top of Workflow Studio core. Pure analytical
  computation; no trade execution.
- Enterprise Platform (https://platform.shivambhaipatel.com): Orchestration across
  Oracle Fusion, Cognos, Power BI, SAP, and Dynamics 365. Spring Boot 3.4 + Next.js 15.
- DealDekho (https://dealdekho.shivambhaipatel.com | Repo: https://github.com/ShivamBhaiPatel/DealDekho):
  Aggregator-first Indian price comparison engine across 6 marketplaces (Amazon, Flipkart,
  Croma, Myntra, etc.) pairing structured price APIs with price verification telemetry
  from the ShopLens browser extension.

## Engineering Trade-Offs & Principles

1. Generative Diffusion vs. Deterministic Skia:
   Diffusion models fail on non-Latin scripts, ligatures, and exact logo reproduction.
   Deterministic Skia provides sub-150ms generation, bit-exact rendering, and zero GPU spend.
2. Aggregator Feeds vs. Raw HTML Scrapers:
   Direct web scrapers break against dynamic DOM changes and bot guards. Pairing official
   aggregator APIs with client-side telemetry from extensions provides resilient price data.
3. Decoupled Core vs. Monolithic Extension:
   Isolating core logic into `@workflow-studio/core` with strict tsconfig Node boundaries
   allows reuse across CLIs, headless runners, and third-party products without editor dependencies.
4. Independent DOM Verification vs. Model Trust:
   Automated browser runners must verify actual DOM state mutations (toasts, modal dismissals,
   server status) rather than trusting an agent or model's self-reported success.
